01.event: While traveling outside Eretz Yisrael, they twice saw a man sowing mixed kinds and one proposed ostracizing him.
01.turn: The other sage rebuffed him each time, saying he did not understand the laws (the first case is permitted outside Eretz Yisrael; the second does not meet Rabbi Yoshiya's standard of sowing wheat, barley and a grape seed in one motion).
01.summary: Two sages walking on a road saw a man planting mixed seeds. One said they should ostracize him, but the other told him he did not understand the law, since this is not forbidden outside Eretz Yisrael. They then saw a man planting wheat and barley among vines and the same exchange followed, with the second sage citing Rabbi Yoshiya to show the man had not sown in the forbidden way. Neither man was ostracized.

02.actor: Rabban Gamliel and a man who came before him
02.event: A man told Rabban Gamliel he had found an open orifice (no sign of virginity) and Rabban Gamliel answered with a parable.
02.turn: Rabban Gamliel suggested the man had perhaps diverted his approach, comparing him to a man in the dark who finds a door open only if he moves the bolt.
02.summary: A man came before Rabban Gamliel and said he had found an open orifice. Rabban Gamliel asked whether he had perhaps diverted his approach and told a parable of a man in the dark who finds a door open only if he moves it. A second version has Rabban Gamliel suggest the man did it intentionally. No result for the man is given.
02.missing: How the case ended; what happened to the man or his claim.

04.event: She seized a saddlebag full of coins for her sustenance.
04.turn: The Sages found they had no power to remove it from her.
04.summary: Rav Dimi reported an incident in which Rabbi Shabbtai's daughter-in-law seized a saddlebag full of coins for her sustenance. The Sages could not take it from her, so she kept it.
04.missing: Any detail beyond a one-line report; it is cited only as legal precedent.

05.actor: A man who betrothed a minor girl, and Ravina
05.event: A man betrothed a minor girl with a bundle of vegetables in the marketplace and Ravina ruled on it.
05.turn: Ravina held the degrading manner of betrothal removed any concern that her father consented.
05.outcome: Ravina ruled the betrothal is not a concern, meaning it is not valid.
05.summary: A man betrothed a minor girl, without her father's consent, using a bundle of vegetables in the marketplace. Ravina ruled that even those who suspect the father may have consented do so only when the betrothal is done respectfully, and this was degrading, so it did not take effect.
05.missing: The people involved, and any real narrative beyond the case and ruling.

06.actor: An Amorite and a resident of Eretz Yisrael
06.event: The Amorite asked how many dates the resident gathers from a palm tree by the Jordan.
06.turn: The Amorite boasted they used to get 120 kor, twice the resident's 60, blaming the Israelites for ruining the land.
06.outcome: The resident replied that he was only describing one side of the tree.
06.summary: An Amorite asked a resident of Eretz Yisrael how much he gathered from a palm tree on the Jordan's bank. The resident said sixty kor. The Amorite said the Israelites had ruined the land, since his people got 120. The resident answered that he had only counted one side of the tree.

07.actor: A creditor, the orphans' herdsman and Rav Nahman
07.event: A creditor seized an ox of orphans and the herdsman disputed when he seized it.
07.turn: Each side told a different story about whether the seizure was before or after the debtor's death; Rav Nahman asked for witnesses and the herdsman had none.
07.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled the creditor could claim he seized it while the debtor was alive, so the seizure stood.
07.summary: A creditor seized an ox from the herdsman of some orphans. The creditor said he took it while the debtor was alive, while the herdsman said it was after death. They went to Rav Nahman, who found the herdsman had no witnesses. He held that since the creditor could claim to have bought it, he could equally claim to have seized it in the debtor's lifetime, so the claim stood.

10.event: A groom told him he found no blood on his wedding night and the bride said she was still a virgin.
10.turn: Rabbi saw they were starving in a drought, so he had them bathed and fed, and sent them back to the room.
10.outcome: The groom then found blood, and Rabbi told him to take possession of his acquisition, quoting Lamentations about their shriveled skin.
10.summary: During a famine a couple came before Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi because the groom found no blood. Rabbi saw their faces were dark from hunger, so he had them bathed, fed and given drink and then sent them into a room. This time the groom found blood and Rabbi told him to go take his bride, quoting a verse about skin shriveled on the bones.

11.event: Abaye rode his donkey along the riverbank and Rav Mesharshiyya and the rabbis on the other bank did not stand for him.
11.turn: Abaye asked whether he was not their primary teacher.
11.outcome: They answered that it had not occurred to them and that they had not seen him.
11.summary: Abaye was riding a donkey along the Sagya River and the rabbis sitting on the other bank did not stand for him. He asked whether he was not their primary teacher, who must be honored from afar. They said they had not noticed him at all.

14.actor: A man who betrothed a minor girl, and Ravina
14.event: A man betrothed a minor girl with a bundle of vegetables in the marketplace and Ravina ruled on it.
14.turn: Ravina held that the degrading manner removed any concern the father consented.
14.outcome: The betrothal is not a concern, meaning it does not take effect.
14.summary: A man betrothed a minor girl, without her father's consent, with a bundle of vegetables in the marketplace. Ravina said that even those who suspect the father consented only apply that to a dignified betrothal, and this one was degrading, so there is no concern.
14.missing: Who the man was, and anything beyond the case and its ruling.

15.actor: A man in Mata Mehasya whose brother's widow fell to him for levirate marriage, and his brother
15.event: The brother wanted to disqualify the yevama from him with a bill of divorce.
15.turn: The man offered to share the inheritance; the brother feared he would be cheated as in the Pumbedita swindler story.
15.outcome: The man offered to let the brother divide the property right away.
15.summary: A man in Mata Mehasya had a yevama fall to him, and his brother wanted to disqualify her with a bill of divorce. The man asked if it was about the estate and promised to split it. The brother feared he would be cheated like the swindler from Pumbedita. The man then offered to let him divide the property from that moment.
15.missing: The earlier Pumbedita story it refers to; whether the brother accepted.

16.actor: Rabbi Hanina bar Hama and Levi
16.event: Rabbi Hanina declined the headship of the yeshiva out of respect for the older Rabbi Afes and sat outside, with Levi studying beside him.
16.turn: Rabbi Afes died and Rabbi Hanina took the head seat, leaving Levi with no one to study with.
16.outcome: Levi traveled to Babylonia, where Rav, hearing of his limping teaching, deduced what had happened.
16.summary: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi appointed Hanina bar Hama to head the yeshiva, but he declined because Rabbi Afes was older. Afes sat at the head and Hanina sat outside, with Levi studying alongside him. When Afes died and Hanina took the head seat, Levi had no one to study with and went to Babylonia. There the people described a limping great man to Rav, who understood from his ruling what had happened.

17.actor: A man who betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags, and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya
17.event: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya examined it before Rav.
17.turn: He checked whether it was worth a peruta, and the Gemara then asked whether a worthless bundle fails to betroth, given Shmuel's opinion.
17.outcome: The betrothal stands only if it was worth a peruta, the question being resolved by distinguishing certain from uncertain betrothal.
17.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags. Rav Shimi bar Hiyya, sitting before Rav, examined it to see if it was worth a peruta, ruling she was betrothed if so and not if not. The Gemara then reconciled this with Shmuel's view by distinguishing certain from doubtful betrothal.
17.missing: The result for the man and woman; it is mostly a legal ruling.

18.actor: A man who rented a donkey, and the renter
18.event: The owner warned the renter not to take the river path, but he went that way and the donkey died.
18.turn: The renter came before Rava and admitted going by the river but said there was no water; Abaye objected that the claim cannot be accepted where there are witnesses.
18.outcome: Rava accepted the renter's claim under the principle 'why would I lie', while Abaye disagreed.
18.summary: A man rented out a donkey and told the renter to avoid the Pekod River path because of water, but the renter went that way and the donkey died. Before Rava, the renter admitted taking that path but said there was no water. Rava accepted his claim since he could have lied and said he took the other path. Abaye objected that this does not apply where witnesses know there is water.

19.actor: Yehuda, son of Rabbi Hiyya, and Rabbi Yannai
19.event: Yehuda studied in the study hall and came home every Shabbat eve with a pillar of fire going before him.
19.turn: One day he was absorbed in his learning and did not come, and Rabbi Yannai, seeing no pillar of fire, concluded he had died.
19.outcome: Rabbi Yannai said to turn his bed over, his words became like an error from a ruler, and Yehuda died.
19.summary: Yehuda, a son-in-law of Rabbi Yannai, came home each Shabbat eve and Rabbi Yannai would see a pillar of fire go before him. One day Yehuda was absorbed in study and did not come. Rabbi Yannai, seeing no sign, said to turn Yehuda's bed over as for a mourner, and that speech took effect and Yehuda died.

20.event: Rav Pappa served drinks at his son's wedding and poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak, son of Rav Yehuda.
20.turn: Rav Yitzhak did not stand before him.
20.summary: At the wedding of his son Abba Mar, Rav Pappa served drinks to the guests. He poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak, son of Rav Yehuda, who did not stand before him. Rav Pappa became angry.
